name: RUST-REF — fprime-rust on FprimeRustReference (native Linux x86_64, fprime-gds)
request_and_goals: "Spin off a child session to fully implement the Rust component integration as seen in fprime-rust and fprime-rust-referenc on JPL-Devin above. You should pull those repos into lestarch-autobot, and get them running. You must use [Used playbook: F Prime Development Campaign — four lanes from request to run-for-record (!fprime_development_campaign)] to ensure the highest quality with those two pieces. Requirements and design are expected to match fprime-python and fprime-python-reference so I DO NOT NEED TOP APPROVE designs or requirements. Run through rfr with seed [withheld]. You must make sure that fprime-rust-reference contains multiple components written in rust and solve the issue where we get duplicate references because rust is baked into each component. All changes can go directly into main of the new autobot repos. Make sure to update to not use fpp-to-json and switch to the new model." "Keep going and driving until we have a working rust implementation." Default goal: a functional Rust-component integration with respect to the description above, proven in system tests (native Linux host, fprime-gds ground system).

tests.title: Image identity
tests.purpose: Confirms the running executable reports the project, framework and library versions recorded in the delivery manifest.
tests.setup: Image installed by flash, GDS attached, ≥ 2 s after start.

rationale.text: the auditor compares the ProjectVersion / LibraryVersions payloads (40-char strings) with the manifest repos[].describe of fprime-rust-reference and fprime-rust

tests.evidence: ProjectVersion, FrameworkVersion and LibraryVersions events whose payloads equal the manifest describe strings.

tests.title: Marker round-trip
tests.purpose: Proves the marker command round-trips through the command path so every later window can be bracketed.

tests.title: Rust command, event and telemetry paths
tests.purpose: Resets and bumps the Rust active component to prove commands dispatch into Rust and events and telemetry come back out.
tests.evidence: ResetIssued, Bumped(7), Bumped(12); Counter 12; no Saturated; no command error.

tests.title: Parameter read from Rust
tests.purpose: Sets THRESHOLD to 5 and bumps past it to prove the Rust handler reads the parameter and saturates on it.

rationale.text: THRESHOLD is re-read on every BUMP, so the set value takes effect without a restart

tests.title: Rust to C++ to Rust port chain
tests.purpose: Bumps the Rust counter and follows the count through the C++ relay into the Rust monitor to prove typed ports in both directions.
tests.setup: L2-1 passed; rustMonitor limit at initial U32::MAX.

rationale.text: RESET and BUMP each send countOut once: Rust→C++ counted by the C++ relay, C++→Rust seen as LastCount

tests.title: Rate-group ports into Rust
tests.purpose: Lets the 1 Hz rate group tick the active Rust component and run the queued Rust component to prove C++ scheduler ports into Rust handlers.

rationale.text: rate group 1 runs at 1 Hz; 5 s window plus bracket sampling admits 4..8 ticks

tests.evidence: TickCount and RunCount each advance 4..8 over the window.

tests.title: Queued Rust command and limit exceedance
tests.purpose: Sets the monitor limit then bumps past it to prove a queued Rust component handles commands and raises a warning event from a relayed count.

rationale.text: the count 10 reaches the queued component on the next run, within the 2 s wait

tests.title: Endurance 60 s
tests.purpose: Runs the deployment for 60 s to prove the Rust components keep servicing rate-group ports with no command errors or counter drift.

rationale.text: 1 Hz over 60 s with scheduler jitter margin

tests.title: Saturation fault path
tests.purpose: Drives the counter into THRESHOLD saturation to prove the Rust warning event and the clamp.
metrics: event rustCounter.Bumped(value=2) precedes event rustCounter.Saturated(value=3, threshold=3)

tests.title: Negative control: SET_LIMIT(0) rejected
tests.purpose: Sends an invalid limit to prove the Rust handler rejects it with a validation error and changes nothing else.

rationale.text: negative control: the rejection is visible at the dispatcher and nothing else happened

tests.evidence: InvalidLimit(0), one OpCodeError(VALIDATION_ERROR), Limit and Exceedances unchanged.

tests.title: Final state
tests.purpose: Resets the counter and reads the installed executable back out of band to leave the deployment in an independently verifiable state.
procedure: action: bench dump reads the installed executable back to {readback}

rationale.text: the reset count 0 travels Rust→C++→Rust one more time

tests.evidence: ResetIssued; Counter 0; Relayed +1; readback sha256 equals the manifest image.
